requirement: An approved master formula must exist for every product AND every batch size. It identifies the product via a code linked to its specification, states dosage form, strength and batch size, lists every starting material with its quantity (calling out any ingredient that is removed during processing), and gives the expected final yield with acceptance limits plus relevant intermediate yields.
system_implications: Master recipe entity keyed by product code + batch size (or an explicitly approved set of discrete sizes); no ad-hoc scaling at batch creation. Bill of materials with quantity per batch and a 'removed during processing' flag (tablets: granulation water/ethanol; injectables: WFI removed by lyophilisation, process gases, declared overages). Mandatory yield targets with lower/upper limits at final and configured intermediate stages. Only masters in Approved/Effective status can be instantiated.
verification_test: Try to create a batch for an unapproved batch size -> rejected. Try to approve a master lacking yield limits or spec-linked product code -> rejected. Flagged evaporating ingredient is listed in the BOM but excluded from theoretical output mass used in yield calculation.

requirement: Processing instructions must cover four themes: (1) setting - location, principal equipment and how critical equipment is readied (including sterilisation where relevant), directly or by reference; (2) readiness - a pre-start confirmation that the workstation holds nothing left from earlier work and that equipment is clean and usable; (3) method and control - ordered steps covering material checks, pre-treatment, order of addition and critical parameters such as time and temperature, plus in-process tests with their limits; (4) holding and safety - bulk storage needs where relevant (container, labelling, special conditions) and any particular precautions.
system_implications: Master step model must carry: room/area and equipment class; equipment-preparation prerequisites evaluated at run time (clean status and clean-hold expiry, calibration due date, assembly check, sterilisation status and sterile-hold expiry for injectables); a mandatory pre-start clearance step; ordered steps with CPP set-points and ranges; IPC definitions with limits; bulk hold definitions (container type, label, storage condition, maximum hold time); precaution text shown and acknowledged at the step. Tablets: granulation end-point, drying temperature/LOD, compression force/hardness. Injectables: SIP/autoclave cycle, filter integrity, bulk solution hold time.
verification_test: Master approval blocked if a CPP has no range or an IPC has no limit. At execution, selecting equipment whose clean or sterile status has expired, or whose calibration is overdue, blocks the step. Bulk hold exceeding maximum time raises an exception.

requirement: Approved packaging instructions are required per product, pack size and pack type, covering (directly or by reference): (1) what is packed - product identity with bulk and finished batch numbers, dosage form, strength and pack content by count, weight or volume; (2) what it is packed with - a complete component list with quantities, sizes, types and specification codes, plus, where appropriate, specimens of printed items showing where batch number and expiry go; (3) readiness - line clearance and inspection of area and equipment before starting, and other precautions; (4) method and control - a description of the operation including significant ancillary operations and equipment, and in-process checks with sampling instructions and acceptance limits.
system_implications: Packaging master keyed by product + pack size + pack type, versioned and approved separately from the processing master. Component BOM with item codes linked to approved specifications and artwork versions; artwork specimen image stored with coding/expiry print zones; mandatory line-clearance checklist template; operation steps with equipment classes; IPC plans with sample size, frequency and limits. Batch record must hold both the bulk batch number consumed and the finished-goods batch number. Tablets: blister/bottle counts, desiccant, leaflet. Injectables: vial/ampoule labels, cartons, tamper evidence, serialization data carriers.
verification_test: Approving a packaging master where a printed component has no linked artwork specimen or no coding zone is blocked. Starting a packaging order is blocked until the clearance checklist is complete. Packaging record shows bulk lot and finished lot linkage.

requirement: A processing record is kept for every batch, generated from the currently approved formula and instructions. Its content falls into four groups: (1) who and when - product and batch identity, dates and times of start, key stages and finish, who performed each significant step and who checked it where relevant, and sign-off by the person responsible for processing; (2) what went in - lot or QC number and actual weighed quantity of each starting material, including any recovered or reprocessed material; (3) how it ran - notable events, main equipment used, in-process results with the tester's identity, and yields at relevant stages; (4) what went wrong - notes on special problems, with signed authorisation for any departure from the instructions.
system_implications: Batch record instance is generated only from the effective master version and stamps that version ID. Automatic server-time stamps at step start/stop and stage milestones. Per-step performer e-signature plus configurable second-person verification. Material consumption captured by lot scan and balance integration (actual weight, not keyed-in theoretical), with a distinct flag and source-batch reference for recovered/reprocessed material. Equipment ID captured per step. IPC results entered against limits with performer ID. Stage and final yields auto-calculated. Deviations linked to the step with authorised signature. Final 'production approval' signature role gates hand-over to QA/QP review.
verification_test: Execute a test batch; confirm master version is recorded, every significant step shows performer and time, weighed lots and actual quantities are present, yields computed, and that production approval cannot be applied while any step is incomplete or any deviation unsigned.

requirement: Where a process is validated and under continuous monitoring and control, automatically generated batch reports may be restricted to a compliance summary together with reports of exceptions and out-of-specification data.
system_implications: Support review-by-exception: a per-batch compliance summary and an exception report listing every out-of-range value, alarm, override, manual entry, correction, deviation and audit-trail change. Only steps configured (under change control, referencing the validation) as validated and continuously monitored may use summary-only reporting; full underlying data is still captured, retained and viewable on drill-down.
verification_test: Run a batch with one injected out-of-limit reading and one manual correction; both must appear in the exception report; data for in-range steps is available on drill-down; attempt to enable summary-only reporting on a step without a validation reference is refused.

requirement: A packaging record is kept for each batch or part-batch packed, derived from the packaging instructions. Content groups: (1) who and when - product and batch identity, dates and times, performers of significant steps and checkers where relevant, and sign-off by the person responsible for packaging; (2) conformity - identity and conformity checks against the instructions, in-process results, and details of the operations with the equipment and lines used; (3) evidence - where possible, specimens of the printed components actually used, including batch coding, expiry and any overprint; (4) exceptions - special problems or unusual events, with signed authorisation of departures; (5) accountability - quantities and identity of printed components and bulk issued, used, destroyed or returned, and the quantity of product obtained, enough to reconcile.
system_implications: Packaging record supports part-batch (sub-lot) records linked to one bulk lot. Captures line ID and equipment IDs, IPC results, and an attached specimen of printed material (scanned sample or vision-system image of the actual coded item). Reconciliation table per printed component and bulk: issued, used, destroyed, returned, plus finished units, samples and rejects. Final approval signature by packaging-responsible role.
verification_test: Complete a packaging run; record contains line ID, IPCs, a specimen image of a coded label/carton, full reconciliation table, and approval; approval is blocked while reconciliation fields are empty (unless the documented electronic-control exemption in EU4-07 is active).

requirement: The quantity reconciliation data for printed components and bulk may be left out of the packaging record only where robust electronic controls operate during packaging and this is justified.
system_implications: Reconciliation is ON by default for every packaging master. Turning it off for a component requires a controlled configuration change that names the electronic control relied on (e.g. 100% code/vision verification with verified reject, roll-fed labels with splice detection, serialization aggregation), references its validation, and is approved by QA. The record then shows the justification reference instead of counts. Serialized injectable/tablet packs: reconcile commissioned vs. decommissioned vs. shipped serial numbers as the electronic equivalent.
verification_test: Attempt to disable reconciliation without a QA-approved justification record -> blocked. With an approved justification, packaging record displays the justification ID; audit trail records who enabled it and when.

requirement: Documentation rules apply whatever the medium (paper, electronic, photographic). Each type of document must be defined and adhered to. Complex systems must be understood, documented, validated and adequately controlled. For hybrid (part paper, part electronic) and single-medium systems alike, the firm must describe how masters, official copies, data processing and the resulting records relate to one another and how each is controlled; electronic templates, forms and masters need appropriate controls; and record integrity must be protected for the entire retention period.
system_implications: eBMR must declare, per record type, which is the official (master) record: electronic record, printout, or combination. Hybrid points (e.g. printed labels, paper chart recorder output, instrument printouts, paper deviation forms) must be formally mapped with a documented linkage (scan attached as true copy, ID cross-reference). Templates/forms in the system are version-controlled, approved and locked. System is validated (Annex 11) and its configuration controlled.
verification_test: Documentation review: a record-type register exists showing official medium per record type. Test that editing a released template is impossible without a new version and approval. Test that a paper attachment carries a unique ID, is linked to the batch and step, and is reviewed as part of the record.

requirement: Documents must be carefully designed, drafted, reviewed and issued, and be consistent with the marketing authorisation and product specification file. Producing working copies from masters must not be able to introduce errors. Documents holding instructions must be approved, signed and dated by authorised people, have clear content and a unique identifier, and state when they take effect; they should be laid out logically, easy to check, and written as directives.
system_implications: Batch record instances are generated programmatically from the approved master (no copy/retype). Master recipe workflow: author -> reviewer(s) -> approver with e-signatures, unique document ID + version, and an effective-from date after which it becomes executable. Optional MA cross-check field (dossier reference / variation number) on the master. Instructions rendered as numbered imperative steps.
verification_test: Confirm the batch record content equals the master content (hash/field comparison) for a generated batch. A master with approval but future effective date cannot be instantiated before that date. Unapproved draft cannot be instantiated.

requirement: Quality-system documents must be reviewed periodically and kept current, and once a document is revised there must be a mechanism that prevents the superseded version from being used by mistake.
system_implications: Masters carry a periodic review due date with alerts; upon approval of a new version the prior version is automatically retired for new batches. Defined rule for batches in progress when a master changes (continue on old version with justification or migrate under change control) and the record shows which version governed each step. Printed forms or labels from superseded versions are invalidated (version/ID printed on every output).
verification_test: Approve v2 of a master; attempt to start a new batch on v1 -> blocked. Check in-flight batch behaviour follows the configured rule and is audit-trailed. Overdue periodic review is flagged on a dashboard.

requirement: Controlled documents themselves should not be handwritten; where data must be entered, adequate space must be provided, and any handwritten entries must be clear, legible and indelible.
system_implications: Every data point in the master has a defined, typed entry field (unit, precision, allowed range or list) so free-text is the exception. Where paper remains (hybrid printouts, emergency paper fallback forms), the printed form is generated from the approved master with enough space for each entry, carries a unique form ID, and is later reconciled into the electronic record. No handwritten master instructions.
verification_test: Master editor refuses a data-entry step without a field definition. Printed fallback form shows batch ID, form ID/page x of y and dedicated fields for every entry; issued fallback forms are counted and all returned forms reconciled.

requirement: Records must be made or completed when each action is performed, so that every significant manufacturing activity can be traced.
system_implications: Timestamps come from a synchronised server clock, never from a user-editable field. Steps are signed at completion; late entries are allowed only via a 'late entry' path that records actual time of activity, time of entry and a mandatory reason, and are flagged for review. Batch-level genealogy links materials, equipment, rooms, people and steps.
verification_test: Attempt to backdate a timestamp -> not possible. Enter a step 2 h after its planned window via late-entry path: record shows both times, reason and a review flag that appears in the exception report.

requirement: Any change to a recorded entry must be signed and dated by the person making it, the original value must remain readable, and a reason must be recorded where appropriate.
system_implications: Corrections never overwrite: the system keeps original value, new value, who, when (server time) and a mandatory reason (pick-list plus free text) in a secure audit trail. Corrections to GMP-relevant data after step sign-off require re-signature and, for critical data (weights, IPC results, CPPs, yields), a second-person or QA approval. Correction history is shown inline in the batch record view and in the exception report.
verification_test: Correct a weighed quantity after signing: original remains visible, reason required, correction appears in the audit trail and exception report, and step is re-signed. Attempt a correction without reason -> blocked. Direct DB update is detectable (audit trail/hash check).

requirement: The firm must define which record belongs to each manufacturing activity and where it is kept, and must have secure controls, validated where appropriate, that keep records intact throughout their retention period.
system_implications: Record-type register inside the system (or linked SOP) mapping each activity to its record and storage location (eBMR DB, archive, attached external systems such as SCADA/historian, LIMS, weighing). Integrity controls: role-based write access, audit trail, backup/restore tested, checksums on archived records, readable-format migration plan. Archive/export produces complete human-readable batch record with metadata and audit trail.
verification_test: Restore a batch record from backup/archive and compare against checksum; record opens with all data, signatures and audit trail intact. Register lists location of every record type referenced by the master.

requirement: Batch documentation must be retained for the longer of: one year beyond the batch expiry date, or at least five years after QP certification of the batch. For investigational medicinal product batches the minimum is five years after the last clinical trial using the batch is completed or formally stopped. Product-specific legislation (e.g. ATMPs) may demand longer periods.
system_implications: Retention engine computes a retention-until date per batch = max(expiry + 1 year, QP certification date + 5 years), stored with the record and recomputed if expiry is extended/changed; IMP batches use a separate rule tied to trial end dates entered by QA; configurable overrides for longer national or product-type rules. Purge/delete of batch records is impossible before that date and requires QA-approved, audit-trailed disposition afterwards. Retention applies to the full record including audit trails, attachments and linked data (e.g. historian extracts).
verification_test: Batch with 24-month shelf life certified 2026-01-10: retention date = 2031-01-10 (5 y after certification exceeds expiry+1 y). Batch with 60-month shelf life: expiry + 1 y governs. Attempt deletion before retention date -> refused and logged.

requirement: Other documents are retained according to the activity they support. Critical documentation, including raw data supporting the marketing authorisation (e.g. validation or stability data), is kept while the authorisation is valid; it may be retired only when superseded by a complete new data set and with a documented justification, and raw data behind process validation must be kept at least as long as the records of every batch released on the basis of that validation.
system_implications: Masters, master versions, recipe change history, and any validation-linked configuration (e.g. the validated state that justifies review-by-exception) are retained at least as long as any batch record that relied on them. Link each batch to the master version and validation references so retention of those objects is automatically extended while dependent batches are retained.
verification_test: Attempt to archive-delete a master version still referenced by a batch within retention -> blocked with a dependency message.

requirement: Written procedures must govern release and rejection of materials and products, especially QP certification of finished product. The QP must be able to see every record, and a mechanism must flag notable observations and any modification of critical data.
system_implications: QP/QA review workspace that exposes the complete batch record plus linked deviations, change controls, lab results and audit trails. Automatic flags for special observations (comments, events, deviations) and for any post-entry change to data classified as critical, so the reviewer sees them without searching. Release status workflow: quarantine -> production approved -> QA reviewed -> QP certified / rejected, each with e-signature.
verification_test: Change a critical data point after completion and add an operator comment: both surface as flags in the QP review screen; QP certification is blocked until each flag is acknowledged.

requirement: Logbooks are required for major or critical production equipment, analytical testing and areas where product is processed, recording in time order the use, calibration, maintenance, cleaning or repair, with dates and the identity of who performed the work.
system_implications: Electronic equipment and room logbooks that are automatically populated from batch execution (usage start/stop with batch and product ID, cleaning events) and from maintenance/calibration modules; entries are chronological and immutable (corrections per EU4-13). Batch step checks equipment/room status from the logbook (last product, clean status, calibration due). Injectables: also autoclave/SIP cycles, filter integrity tests, isolator/RABS decontamination. Tablets: compression machine tooling (punch/die sets) usage.
verification_test: Run two batches on the same granulator/filling line; logbook shows both usages and the intervening cleaning in chronological order with performer IDs; attempt to insert a back-dated logbook entry without the late-entry path fails.

requirement: Consolidated signature points in the in-force Chapter 4: authorised persons approve, sign and date instruction documents; alterations are signed and dated; batch processing and packaging records identify who performed each significant step and, where relevant, who checked it; departures from instructions carry a signed authorisation; and the person responsible for processing or packaging approves the completed record. The 2011 chapter does not describe how electronic signatures work; that comes from Annex 11 (section 14, 2011), which was not re-checked in this task.
system_implications: Signature catalogue built into the product with one configurable signature type per point: master approval, correction, step performed, step verified, deviation authorisation, production/packaging record approval, QA review, QP certification. Each type defines the allowed roles, whether the signer must differ from earlier signers on the same object, and whether re-authentication is needed. Every signature event is recorded in the audit trail and shown in the rendered record.
verification_test: For each signature type, test: correct role accepted, wrong role refused, the same person refused where independence is required, and the signature (name, date-time, meaning) appears in the rendered batch record and audit trail.

requirement: In the chapter, 'written' covers data recorded on any medium, provided it can be rendered in human-readable form. Records must give the history of each manufactured batch, including its distribution. Controls must keep documents accurate, intact, available and legible.
system_implications: Every electronic batch record, including its metadata, attachments and audit trail, can be rendered on demand as a complete human-readable report (screen and PDF/print) for inspectors and the QP, for the whole retention period. The batch genealogy can be linked to distribution data held in ERP, so the history of a batch can be traced forward to customers for recall.
verification_test: Render an archived batch record: every step, value, signature, comment, deviation link and audit-trail entry is present and legible. From a finished batch ID, a forward trace returns its distribution records.

requirement: Moving a GMP activity from paper/manual handling onto a computerised system must not lower product quality, weaken process control or dilute quality assurance, and must not raise the overall process risk. The application software has to be validated and the IT infrastructure it runs on has to be qualified.
system_implications: Every control that exists in the paper BMR (line clearance sign-off, second-person checks, yield reconciliation, label reconciliation, in-process checks) needs an equal or stronger electronic control in the eBMR. The vendor/customer must be able to deliver validation evidence for the configured application (recipes, workflows, calculations, interfaces) and qualification evidence for servers, database, network and any cloud tenancy.
verification_test: Inspect a paper-to-electronic control mapping matrix: each paper control maps to a named system control and at least one executed test case. Confirm approved infrastructure qualification records and application validation summary report exist for the release under test.

requirement: Risk management must be applied across the whole system lifecycle, weighing patient safety, data integrity and product quality; how far validation and data-integrity controls go must be decided on a documented, justified risk basis.
system_implications: The eBMR should let the regulated user tag each data field / step with a criticality class (e.g., critical process parameter, GMP-relevant, informational) and drive controls from that tag: second-person verification, mandatory reason-for-change, audit-trail review flags, and exception reporting. The risk assessment behind the classification must be stored/linked as a controlled document. Injectables will typically classify more steps as critical (aseptic interventions, sterilisation, filtration, environmental monitoring excursions) than tablets.
verification_test: Pick a sample of recipe steps; confirm each has a criticality classification traceable to an approved risk assessment and that the behaviour (e.g., witness required) changes when the classification changes, under change control.

requirement: The company must keep a current inventory of its GMP-relevant systems and what GMP functions they perform; for critical systems it must also maintain an up-to-date description covering physical and logical layout, data flows, interfaces to other systems or processes, hardware/software prerequisites and security measures.
system_implications: The eBMR vendor must supply (and keep current per release) an architecture/system description: modules, database, integration points (ERP/material management, LIMS, weighing scales, SCADA/PLC, historian, label printers, QMS for deviations), data flow diagrams, and security design. The system should be able to export its own configuration inventory (interfaces enabled, versions) to help keep the description current.
verification_test: Compare the documented interface list with the interfaces actually configured in the production instance; any undocumented interface is a failure. Confirm the description is version-controlled and was updated at the last change.

requirement: When data move to another format or another system, validation must show that neither the values nor the meaning of the data changed during the migration.
system_implications: Upgrades, database migrations, archive exports and legacy-record imports must include automated reconciliation: record counts, checksums/hashes per record, field-level comparison of values and units, and preservation of audit trail, signatures and metadata. Signature manifestations and audit-trail links must survive migration and remain bound to the same records.
verification_test: Run a migration on a validation copy; compare source vs target record counts and hashes; spot-check that audit trails, e-signature meaning/date/time, units and precision are unchanged; confirm the migration report is approved before go-live.

requirement: Where critical data are keyed in by hand, a further accuracy check is needed, done either by a second person or by an electronic means that has itself been validated; how critical a value is, and what a wrong entry could cause, must be judged through risk management.
system_implications: For fields classified critical (e.g., dispensed weight typed manually, lot number of an API, compression force set-point, fill volume/weight, sterilisation cycle parameters, filter integrity test result), the eBMR must either (a) capture the value directly from the instrument/scale/PLC or verify it by barcode scan against the expected item, or (b) force an independent second-user verification with its own authentication before the step can be completed. The verifier must be a different user from the performer (system-enforced), and both identities, timestamps and the verified value are stored.
verification_test: Configure a critical manual field; attempt to complete the step without verification (must block); attempt verification by the same user (must be rejected); verify by a second user and check the audit record holds both identities and times. Test that a barcode mismatch blocks progression.

requirement: Stored data must be protected against damage by both physical and electronic measures, must be checked to stay accessible, readable and accurate, and must remain accessible for the entire retention period.
system_implications: Database and file storage must sit on protected, redundant infrastructure; the system should provide integrity checking (e.g., record-level hashes or database consistency checks) and a retrievability check that proves old batch records can still be opened and rendered with their audit trail and signatures. Retention rules per record type (EU batch documentation: at least one year beyond expiry or five years after QP certification, whichever is longer, per EU GMP Chapter 4) must be configurable and must block premature deletion.
verification_test: Restore/open a batch record older than the current software version and confirm full rendering incl. audit trail and signatures; attempt to delete a record inside its retention period (must be blocked); review the output of the periodic integrity/readability check.

requirement: All relevant data must be backed up regularly; the integrity and accuracy of backups and the ability to restore them must be proven during validation and then monitored periodically.
system_implications: Backups must cover the database, attachments, configuration (recipes/master batch records, user/role definitions) and audit trails as a consistent set. Restore procedures must be documented and exercised; the system should log backup job success/failure and alert on failure. Point-in-time recovery objectives should be set by risk (an injectable line running continuous aseptic filling needs a tight recovery point so in-progress batch data are not lost).
verification_test: Perform a restore of a production backup into an isolated environment; compare record counts/hashes and open a sample of batch records with audit trails; confirm backup failure raises an alert; confirm restore test records exist at the defined frequency.

requirement: It must be possible to produce clear paper copies of electronically held data; for records that support batch release, the printout must be able to show whether any data were altered after they were first entered.
system_implications: The eBMR needs a controlled print/export of the executed batch record (human-readable, complete, paginated, with unique record ID, version and 'page x of y') in which every value that was modified after first entry is visibly flagged, ideally with original value, new value, who, when and why, or a cross-reference to the audit trail entry. The rendered copy must also show signatures with name, date/time and meaning.
verification_test: Enter a value, correct it with a reason, then generate the batch release printout/PDF: the corrected field must be flagged and the original value and change details must be visible or referenced. Confirm unchanged fields are not flagged and that the print is complete (no truncated fields).

requirement: Systems that swap data electronically with other systems need suitable built-in checks so that data are entered and processed correctly and securely, keeping the risk of corruption or loss low.
system_implications: Every interface (ERP/material status, LIMS results, balances, PLC/SCADA, historian, label printing, QMS deviations) must validate what it receives: message schema and completeness, identity matching (material code, lot, batch ID), unit and range checks, duplicate/sequence detection, acknowledgement and retry, and authenticated/encrypted transport. Failed or rejected transfers must raise a visible alert and must never silently drop or default a value into the batch record.
verification_test: Inject malformed, out-of-range, duplicate and wrong-batch messages at each interface; confirm rejection, alerting and logging. Interrupt the connection mid-transfer and confirm no partial or duplicated values land in the batch record.

requirement: Based on risk, the system should itself generate a record of every GMP-relevant change and deletion (an audit trail); the reason for changing or deleting GMP-relevant data must be captured; audit trails must be retrievable, convertible into a form people can understand, and reviewed on a regular basis.
system_implications: Every create/modify/delete of GMP data in the eBMR (step results, parameters, material entries, comments, status changes, signatures, voids) must write an append-only, system-generated entry holding user ID and full name, date/time with time zone, record/field identity, old value, new value and a mandatory reason (reason list plus free text). Ordinary users and administrators must not be able to edit, delete or switch off the trail; the trail must be viewable and exportable in plain language (not only raw database codes), filterable by batch, and flagged for review.
verification_test: Change and delete sample GMP values with each role; confirm entries appear with old/new value, reason, user and timestamp; confirm the save is blocked without a reason; attempt to edit/delete audit entries and to disable auditing via UI, API and admin console (all must fail or, for privileged DB access, be detectable via integrity hashes).

requirement: Any change to the computerised system, including changes to its configuration, may only be made in a controlled way following a defined procedure.
system_implications: Master batch records/recipes, workflows, calculations, limits, role definitions and interface settings must be version-controlled objects with draft-review-approve-effective states, e-signed approvals, and an audit trail of configuration changes. Only one effective version of a master record may be usable for new batches; in-flight batches must stay bound to the version they started on unless an approved change says otherwise. Software releases must go through a test environment before production.
verification_test: Edit a master recipe: confirm it cannot be used in production until approved; confirm running batches keep their original version; confirm configuration audit trail shows who changed what; confirm production configuration cannot be changed directly without the controlled path.

requirement: Systems must be re-assessed at intervals to confirm they are still validated and GMP-compliant; where relevant the review looks at current functionality, deviations, incidents and problems, upgrade history, performance, reliability, security and the validation status.
system_implications: The eBMR should make periodic review easy by providing reports for the review period: configuration and software changes, incident/error logs, interface failures, user-access changes and privileged activity, backup/restore results, performance/uptime, open validation gaps. These reports must be generated by the system (not hand-assembled) to be trustworthy.
verification_test: Generate the periodic-review report pack for a defined period and cross-check a sample of entries against the underlying logs; confirm the pack covers all listed topics.

requirement: Access must be limited to authorised people by physical and/or logical means (e.g., personal credentials, biometrics, access cards, locked server/storage areas); how strong these controls are should reflect how critical the system is; granting, modifying and withdrawing access rights must be recorded.
system_implications: Individual named accounts with role-based permissions (operator, verifier/witness, supervisor, QA reviewer, QP, master-data author, administrator); user administration workflow that logs every grant/change/revocation with requester, approver, date and reason; history of who held which role on any past date must be queryable. Shop-floor terminals in cleanrooms (injectables, Grade A/B gowned operators) need an authentication method usable with gloves (badge/RFID + PIN or biometrics) without resorting to shared logins.
verification_test: Create, modify and disable a user; confirm each action is logged with approver; query role membership as of a past date; confirm a disabled user cannot log in or sign; confirm there is no generic/shared account with write access.

requirement: Data and document management systems must be built so that the identity of whoever enters, changes, confirms or deletes data is recorded together with the date and time.
system_implications: Each recorded value and each confirmation (e.g., 'performed', 'verified', 'checked') must carry the authenticated user identity and a trusted server timestamp (not a client-device clock the operator can change). Timestamps should be synchronised to a reliable time source and stored with time-zone information so multi-site data line up.
verification_test: Change a terminal clock and record a step: the stored timestamp must still come from the synchronised server source. Confirm every entry, verification and deletion in a test batch shows user identity and date/time.

requirement: All incidents, not just outright system failures or data errors, must be reported and assessed; for critical incidents the root cause must be found and used as the basis for corrective and preventive action.
system_implications: The eBMR must log technical and functional incidents (interface failures, lost connections, crashes during a step, failed signatures, time-sync failures, printing failures) in a way that links them to affected batches, so an incident can be raised in the QMS and its batch impact assessed before release. Batches touched by an open incident should be flagged on the release/QP view.
verification_test: Simulate an interface outage during a weighing step; confirm an incident/event record is created, linked to the batch, and shown as open on the batch review/QP screen until closed.

requirement: Electronic records may be signed electronically. Such signatures must carry, inside the company, the same weight as a handwritten one; they must stay permanently tied to the record they sign; and they must show when (date and time) they were applied.
system_implications: Signing must require the signer's own credentials at the moment of signing; the signature object (user ID, printed full name, date/time with zone, meaning such as performed/verified/reviewed/approved/certified) must be stored bound to the exact record version (e.g., via record hash), must display on screen and on every rendered copy, and cannot be copied, moved or re-used on another record. A company policy/attestation that users accept e-signatures as equivalent to handwritten ones should be captured in the system (acknowledgement at account activation).
verification_test: Sign a step, then inspect storage: signature references the record version/hash; try to transplant a signature to another record via API/DB manipulation (must be rejected or detected); confirm signature manifestation appears on screen and on the printout with name, date/time and meaning.

requirement: If the computerised system records certification and batch release, it must permit only Qualified Persons to certify release, must clearly identify and record who released or certified each batch, and this act must be done with an electronic signature.
system_implications: A distinct 'QP certification' permission, granted only to persons named as QP on the manufacturing/import authorisation (with an approval workflow and a register of QP accounts). Certification is an e-signature with the meaning 'certified by QP' and the QP's identity; release status changes (quarantine to certified/released) must be possible only through this action and must feed downstream systems (ERP/warehouse) to lift quarantine. Other users, including admins and QA reviewers without QP status, must not be able to certify.
verification_test: Attempt certification with QA reviewer, supervisor and admin accounts (must fail); certify with a QP account and confirm the record shows QP name, date/time, meaning; confirm ERP stock status changes only after certification.

requirement: For systems that support critical processes, arrangements must exist to keep those processes going if the system breaks down (for example a manual or alternative system); how fast the fallback must be in place is set by risk and by the process it supports; the arrangements must be documented and tested.
system_implications: Provide a validated downtime mode: controlled pre-printed/printable emergency batch record sheets generated from the current master record (uniquely numbered, reconciled), local buffering on the shop floor for short network outages with guaranteed ordered re-sync, and a controlled back-entry procedure after recovery where late-entered data are flagged as transcribed from paper, second-person verified, and linked to the scanned original. Injectables: an aseptic filling run cannot simply stop, so fallback must be immediate and pre-staged; tablets may tolerate a planned pause at defined hold points.
verification_test: Execute a downtime drill: cut the network mid-batch, continue on the fallback, restore, back-enter data; confirm back-entered values are flagged, verified, linked to scanned originals and time-stamped with both the original execution time and the entry time.

requirement: Data may be moved to an archive; archived data must be checked for accessibility, readability and integrity, and before relevant changes to the system (hardware or software) the ability to retrieve archived data must be confirmed and tested.
system_implications: Archive function that moves completed, released batch records (with full audit trail, signatures, attachments and metadata) into read-only storage, with fixity checks (hashes) run periodically and a restore/re-render capability that still works after application upgrades. Upgrade validation must include retrieval tests of archived records from earlier versions.
verification_test: Archive a batch, run fixity check, then upgrade the application in a test environment and retrieve/render the archived record; confirm content, audit trail and signatures are intact and hashes match.

requirement: Process owner, system owner, QPs and IT must work closely together and everyone must have suitable qualifications, access level and defined responsibilities. When third parties supply or run the system (including hosting/service providers), formal written agreements must set out responsibilities; supplier competence and reliability are key selection factors and the need for a supplier audit is set by risk; the supplier's quality information and audit findings must be available to inspectors on request.
system_implications: Roles for process owner and system owner should be configurable in the system and shown on validation/periodic review outputs. For a SaaS or vendor-hosted eBMR: a quality/technical agreement covering data ownership, backup, change notification, incident reporting, audit-trail retention, access for inspections and exit/data return; the vendor should support customer audits and provide release notes and validation packages.
verification_test: Check the quality agreement covers the listed topics; confirm the vendor audit report is on file with a risk-based rationale; confirm the system shows named process and system owners.

requirement: User requirements must describe the needed functions, be grounded in documented risk assessment and GMP impact, and be traceable across the lifecycle. Validation must show suitable test methods and scenarios, paying particular attention to process parameter limits, data limits and error handling; automated test tools and test environments need a documented assessment of their adequacy.
system_implications: Maintain a URS-to-test traceability matrix per configured product/recipe. The eBMR must enforce configured limits (warning vs action/reject limits for weights, in-process results, CPPs) and must handle errors deterministically (e.g., instrument disconnect, invalid barcode, double submission) - all of which must be tested, including boundary values. If automated/regression testing tools are used, keep an assessment of their fitness.
verification_test: Boundary tests on each critical limit (just inside, on, just outside); negative tests for error paths; review traceability matrix completeness; confirm the test-tool assessment exists.

source: EU GMP Chapter 4 Documentation (2011, in force)
requirement: Documents and records can be partly electronic and partly paper; for both mixed and single-format systems the company must state how master documents, official copies, data handling and records relate to each other and how each is controlled.
system_implications: The eBMR configuration must define which object is the master (the approved electronic master batch record/recipe), which outputs are official copies (controlled PDFs/prints, watermarked 'copy' with generation date and version), and which is the original record of execution (the electronic record with its audit trail). Any remaining paper elements (e.g., printed labels, instrument printouts, EM plates) need a defined link to the electronic batch (scan + reconciliation + reference ID).
verification_test: Review the documented record map; print a copy and confirm it is marked as an uncontrolled/official copy with version and date; confirm each paper artefact type has a defined linkage and reconciliation check in the eBMR.

source: EU GMP Chapter 4 Documentation (2011, in force)
requirement: Batch documentation has to be kept for one year beyond the expiry date of the batch or for at least five years after QP certification, whichever period ends later.
system_implications: Retention end date must be computed per batch as the later of (expiry + 1 year) and (QP certification date + 5 years), be longer if other markets or company policy require it, and block purge/archiving-with-deletion before that date. Audit trails, signatures and metadata inherit the same retention as the batch record.
verification_test: For test batches with different expiry and certification dates, verify the computed retention date; attempt deletion before the date (blocked, logged).

source: EU GMP Chapter 4 Documentation (2011, in force)
requirement: Records are to be made or completed as each action is performed, and any alteration to an entry must be signed and dated, must leave the original information readable, and where appropriate must state why it was changed.
system_implications: Entry screens must record the actual execution time automatically; entries made materially later than the step (configurable threshold) are flagged as late with a mandatory justification. Corrections never overwrite: the prior value stays visible in history and on the review/print rendering, and the correction carries user e-signature, timestamp and reason. No 'edit in place' for executed steps without this correction workflow.
verification_test: Complete a step, then correct a value: confirm prior value remains visible on screen/PDF with correction signature, time and reason; back-date attempt through UI/API is impossible; late entry beyond threshold forces justification.

clause: 3.3, 4.2, 4.5, 4.6 (supplier documentation; validation records; supplier QMS; bespoke systems)
requirement: Documentation shipped with commercial off-the-shelf products must be reviewed by the regulated user to check it meets user requirements; validation documentation should include change-control records and reports on deviations found during validation; the regulated user must take reasonable steps to ensure the system was developed under an appropriate quality management system and assess the supplier accordingly; for bespoke or customised systems there should be a process for formal assessment and reporting of quality and performance measures across all lifecycle stages.
system_implications: eBMR vendors should provide a validation package (requirements, design/configuration specs, test evidence, release notes, known-issues list) and evidence of their development QMS (SDLC, code review, testing, defect management). Customer-specific extensions (custom scripts, reports, interfaces) must be treated as bespoke and carry their own lifecycle quality metrics and test evidence. Validation deviations must be recorded and resolved before release.
verification_test: Review the vendor package and audit report for SDLC evidence; confirm custom extensions have their own specifications and test results; confirm validation deviations are logged and closed or justified in the validation summary.

source: EU GMP Annex 11 (2011) and EMA GMP Q&A: data integrity
clause: Annex 11 section 9 (audit trails) and 8.2 (printouts for batch release); EMA Q&A on review of audit trails as part of data review
requirement: Based on risk, systems should create a record of every GMP-relevant change and deletion (an audit trail), and the reason for each change or deletion of GMP data must be documented. Audit trails must be available, convertible into a readable form and reviewed regularly. Printed copies of records that support batch release must show whether any data were changed after the original entry. Under EU expectations (EMA Q&A, PIC/S PI 041), changes to critical data should be assessed as part of routine review before the batch is released.
system_implications: The system keeps an immutable audit trail of who, what, when, old value, new value and reason for every create, modify, delete, void, status change and signature on batch data. A reason is mandatory for any change to a committed GMP value. The batch review screen and release printout have a clear 'data changed after entry' indicator for each changed value, plus a batch-scoped, human-readable audit-trail report filtered to GMP-relevant events on critical data. Audit-trail review is a signed, mandatory step in batch review, and release (or QP certification) is blocked until it is done. Audit trails cannot be switched off by users.
verification_test: Change a critical value with a reason and check the release printout marks it as changed, and the audit-trail report shows old value, new value, user, time and reason. Try to release without the audit-trail review signature and check it is blocked. Try to disable audit trailing as an administrator and check it is impossible or is itself logged and alarmed.

source: EU GMP Part I Chapter 4 (2011) Documentation
clause: 4.20 - Batch Processing Record (incl. note on compliance summaries/exception reports)
requirement: Each processed batch needs a processing record built from the relevant parts of the currently approved manufacturing formula and processing instructions, prepared in a way that avoids transcription errors. Summary of what it must hold: product and batch identity; start time, times of key intermediate stages and finish time; who did each significant step and, where relevant, who checked it; lot or control numbers and actual quantities of every starting material weighed, including any recovered or reprocessed material added; relevant operations or events and major equipment used; IPC results with who did them; yields at pertinent stages; notes on special problems, with signed authorisation for any departure from the formula or instructions; and approval by the person responsible for processing. For a validated process under continuous monitoring and control, automatically generated reports may be limited to compliance summaries and exception or OOS reports.
system_implications: The executable batch record is generated automatically from the effective, approved MBR version, with no re-keying of instructions. Its version ID appears on every page and in the output. Mandatory structured fields cover all the content groups above, with server-side timestamps for start, key stages and finish, and user identity for performer and checker (checker must be a different person). Material lots and actual weights come from dispensing and scanning. Equipment IDs are scanned with status checks. Yield calculations are automatic at defined stages with alert limits. Any departure needs a deviation record with QA authorisation. Final production approval is by e-signature from the responsible role. For continuously monitored automated steps (for example a tablet press with automated weight control, or an isolator filling line with integrated monitoring), the record may store a validated compliance summary plus exceptions, while the full data stay retrievable.
verification_test: Generate a batch record and check it matches the effective MBR version exactly (compare step lists and limits). Try to complete a step with the same user as performer and checker and check it is blocked. Check yields calculate and alert. For an automated step, check the compliance summary and exception list are produced and the full underlying data can be retrieved from the record.

source: EU GMP Part I Chapter 4 (2011) Documentation
requirement: Each batch or part-batch packaged needs a packaging record based on the packaging instructions. Summary of contents: product and batch identity; dates and times of packaging; who did and who checked each significant step; identity and conformity checks against the instructions, including IPC results; details of the operations with the equipment and lines used; specimens of the printed packaging material used where possible (including coded batch and expiry prints); notes on unusual events with signed authorisation of any departure; quantities and identity of printed packaging materials and bulk issued, used, destroyed or returned, with product yield, to allow reconciliation; and approval by the person responsible for packaging. Where robust electronic controls are in place during packaging, there may be justification for not including some of this detail, such as reconciliation.
system_implications: The packaging record has line-clearance checks (signed and verified) before start. Printed components are issued and returned by barcode scan with lot IDs and counts. Coding and overprint text (batch, expiry and, where used, serialisation data) is captured as an image or data specimen and verified against expected values. Vision and reject-station counts come from the line. Automatic reconciliation compares issued, used, destroyed and returned counts with limits, and any breach becomes a deviation. Any MBR decision to reduce manual reconciliation because of electronic controls must reference the validated control and a risk assessment. Tablets: blister or bottle lines. Injectables: vial or ampoule labelling and cartoning after visual inspection.
verification_test: Run a packaging batch with a deliberate label count mismatch above the limit and check a deviation is raised and packaging approval is blocked. Check the specimen of the coded batch and expiry print is stored and compared with the expected values. Check line clearance must be completed and verified before the first packaging step can start.

source: EU GMP Part I Chapter 4 (2011) Documentation
requirement: Records must be made or completed when each action is done, so that all significant manufacturing activities can be traced. Any change to an entry must be signed and dated, the original information must stay readable, and the reason for the change should be recorded where appropriate.
system_implications: Timestamps come from a synchronised server clock, not the client device. Each entry records who did the action and when, and the system flags entries made more than a configured interval after the step's actual execution (late entries), requiring a reason and showing them in the exception report. Corrections never overwrite: the original stays visible in the record view and the printout, and the correction stores user, time and a mandatory reason chosen from a controlled list plus optional free text. Back-dating is impossible.
verification_test: Try to change the client clock and check recorded times stay server-based. Enter a value after the configured late-entry window and check a reason is required and the entry is flagged. Correct a value and check the original stays visible alongside the correction with user, time and reason.

source: EU GMP Part I Chapter 4 (2011) Documentation
clause: 4.10 - record location and integrity over retention; 4.11 - retention periods
requirement: It must be clear which record belongs to each manufacturing activity and where it is kept. Secure (and, where appropriate, validated) controls must protect each record's integrity for its whole retention period. Batch documentation must be kept for at least one year after the batch expires or five years after QP certification, whichever is later. Investigational product batch records are kept at least five years after the last trial using the batch ends. Raw data from process validation are kept at least as long as the records of any batch released on the strength of that validation. Critical documentation supporting the marketing authorisation is kept while the authorisation is valid.
system_implications: Each batch record (including audit trail, signatures, attachments, exception reports and linked deviations) gets a computed retention date: the later of expiry plus 1 year and QP certification date plus 5 years, extended by any configured longer rule (market law, validation linkage, clinical use). Deletion or purge before that date is technically blocked. Archive and migration keep the record readable with its metadata and audit trail, and are verified. Validation datasets are linked to the batches they support, so their retention extends automatically. A record-location register shows where each record type is held.
verification_test: Create a batch with a 24-month expiry certified today and check the computed retention date equals the later of the two rules. Try to purge it and check the purge is blocked. Link the batch to a validation report and check the report's retention date extends to cover the batch. Restore an archived record and check the audit trail and signatures are intact and readable.

source: EU GMP Part I Chapter 4 (2011) Documentation
clause: Principle and 4.1-4.4 - hybrid and homogeneous systems; control of templates, masters and reproduced documents; approval of instructions
requirement: Documentation may be paper, electronic or a hybrid of both. For each system, the firm must state how master documents, official copies, data handling and records relate and are controlled. Electronic templates, forms and master documents need suitable controls. Working copies made from masters must not introduce errors. Documents containing instructions must be approved, signed and dated by authorised people.
system_implications: For every record type, the system configuration or SOP register states which form is the official (master) record: electronic, paper or defined hybrid parts. MBRs (masters) are approved by e-signature of the authorised roles (for example production, QA and, where required, regulatory) before becoming effective. Executed batch records are generated from the master by the system, never retyped. Any printed copy carries 'copy' status, the source version and the print time, and cannot be used as the official record unless issued through the controlled-form route (see EMA-DI-05).
verification_test: Check the configuration lists the official-record designation for batch records, logbooks and forms. Try to make an MBR effective without all required approval signatures and check it is blocked. Print a batch record page and check it is marked as a copy with version and time.

requirement: Within the company, an electronic record may be signed electronically, and that signature carries the same weight as a handwritten one. It must be permanently linked to its record and include the time and date it was applied. When a computerised system records batch certification and release, only Qualified Persons may be able to certify release, and the system must clearly identify and record who did it, using an electronic signature.
system_implications: Each e-signature is cryptographically or relationally bound to the exact record version signed and shows the signer's name, date, time and meaning (performed, verified, reviewed, approved, certified). Editing signed content invalidates the signature and requires re-signing. The certify/release action is available only to users holding the QP role (EU) or the authorised QA-release role (US), is checked at execution time, and records the signer. Release is blocked while open items remain (see Q10-03 and A11-01).
verification_test: Try to certify a batch as a user without the QP role and check it is refused. Sign a record, change a signed value through the correction workflow, and check the signature is marked invalid and re-signing is required. Check the printout and screen show signer, date/time and meaning.

clause: Section 5 (data: built-in checks for entry, processing and electronic exchange) and section 6 (accuracy checks for critical manual entries)
requirement: Systems that exchange data electronically need built-in checks that data are entered, processed and transferred correctly and securely. Critical data entered by hand need an extra accuracy check, either by a second person or by a validated electronic method. How critical the data are, and what an entry error could cause, should be judged through risk management.
system_implications: Field-level validation covers type, range, format and unit. Barcode or RFID identity checks cover materials, equipment, rooms and containers, and a mismatch prevents the step from continuing. Interface transfers (ERP material master, LIMS results, scales, SCADA/historian) use checksums or acknowledgments with reconciliation, and failed transfers raise alerts. Any critical value keyed in by hand, as determined by the field's criticality attribute (see EMA-DI-02), requires independent second-person verification by e-signature, unless a validated electronic check covers it (for example a direct balance interface). Tablet examples: API potency-adjusted quantity, granulation fluid amount. Injectable examples: compounding volumes, filter-integrity test values typed from an off-line tester, sterilisation load IDs.
verification_test: Scan a wrong material lot at dispensing and check the step is blocked. Key in a critical value manually and check the step cannot close without a second, different user's verification. Corrupt an interface message in the test environment and check the transfer is rejected and alerted.

source: EU GMP Annex 11 (2011); EMA GMP Q&A: data integrity
clause: Annex 11 section 12 (security: physical/logical access control, recording of access changes, identity of operators) and section 4.8/5 (validated interfaces); EMA Q&A on data governance and access
requirement: Physical and logical controls must restrict access to authorised people, with the extent of control depending on how critical the system is. Granting, changing and removing access must be recorded. Records management must capture who entered, changed, confirmed or deleted data, and when. Under EU data-integrity expectations, access should be role-based and each user uniquely identified. Administrator rights should be restricted and kept apart from routine GMP data entry, so that nobody can change data they generate without detection.
system_implications: Every account belongs to one named person, with no shared or generic GMP accounts. Roles are role-based (operator, verifier, supervisor, QA reviewer, QP/QA release, MBR author, MBR approver, system administrator). Separation of duties is enforced: administrators cannot sign GMP steps, MBR authors cannot approve their own MBRs, and performers cannot verify their own entries. Account and role changes are logged and reviewed periodically, with the review recorded. Sessions lock after inactivity, and signing requires re-entry of credentials.
verification_test: Try to assign both the administrator and operator-signing roles to one account and check it is blocked or flagged by the separation-of-duties rule. Check the access-change log records who granted what and when. Check an MBR author cannot approve their own MBR. Check the inactivity lock and re-authentication at signing.
